approved: Aviation Consumer Protection (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2026
Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that would create an Aviation Consumer Protection Framework to improve air travel for passengers.
The framework would let the Minister set minimum service standards for airlines and airports, monitored by a new body called the Aviation Consumer Protection Authority.
A separate Aviation Consumer Ombuds Scheme would handle complaints, and an Aircraft Noise Ombudsperson would review noise complaints against Airservices Australia and the Department of Defence.
Establishes a regulatory framework for aviation consumer protections.
Enables the Minister to issue an Aviation Consumer Protections Charter with minimum standards.
Creates the Aviation Consumer Protection Authority for monitoring and enforcement.
Sets up the Aviation Consumer Ombuds Scheme for dispute resolution.
Establishes the Aircraft Noise Ombudsperson to review noise complaint handling.
Aviation consumers, airlines, airport operators, Airservices Australia, and the Department of Defence.
